attempts.summary: Implemented HTTPS-on-8443 with auto-renewing certificates on node1 using an Ansible playbook run from node2 (the control node, identified because it had ansible pre-installed with an SSH keypair; node1 did not have ansible). Enabled sshd on node1 (installed but inactive, missing host keys) and authorized node2's key to establish the control path. The role installs nginx + openssl, deploys a POSIX renewal script driven by a systemd oneshot service + timer (30s cadence) that uses `openssl x509 -checkend` against a threshold tuned so the 1-day self-signed cert renews well before its real expiry, atomically replaces the cert/key, and reloads nginx (graceful reload, no dropped connections) whenever a new cert is installed. Verified a live automatic renewal cycle end-to-end: cert serial changed from 12F268... to 068B3E... via the timer (not manual intervention) while a concurrent 60-second curl probe loop against the HTTPS endpoint returned 200 on all 60 requests spanning the rotation, and a fresh TLS handshake afterward served the new certificate. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id + health on both nodes, rebooted node1 first (boot_id changed 1e0cb179→2ce125db) and confirmed nginx, the renewal timer, HTTPS response, and the persisted certificate all recovered; then rebooted node2 (boot_id changed c030bd0d→4439e06f) and confirmed Ansible tooling and control-path recovery via an idempotent playbook re-run (all tasks reported `ok`, zero changes) while node1's service remained continuously healthy.
